newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-BTR profit seen sliding and div cut.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-BTR profit seen sliding and div cut.

text.p: BTR Plc, the rambling comglomerate empire in the throes of a major shake-up, is set to announce a sickly set of interim results next Thursday, say analysts who forecast falling profits and a slashed dividend.

Market watchers are also desperate for news on how chief executive Ian Strachan will take the company's strategy forward and tackle BTR's cash flow problems - issues which have led to the value of the shares slumping 25 percent in 1996.
The interim profits are expected by many analysts to fall 15 percent to around 600 million, from 729 million in 1995.
The interim payout is seen collapsing by one third from 1995's 5.54 pence per share level.
Most analysts say a fall in profits and dividend of this magnitude has already been priced in after a lengthy and painful debate over the summer.

But Colin Porter, analyst at Albert E Sharp, said "A clear restructuring comment has got to come through to reassure the market. The worst of all possible worlds would be if BTR holds the dividend and says at the final dividend stage it will make a decision. That would mean another six months of no-man's land.
Failure to provide it could see shares revisit their 1996 low of around 225p from the current 258p level, said Porter.
One analyst said this week: "There is a myriad of unanswered issues - Strategy, dividend policy, restructuring. There is a major information vacuum to be filled."
Tilcon has begun restructuring already by selling non-core businesses - amounting to 20 percent of the group sales.

BTR is currently a sprawling mass of interests, with 1,000 businesses spanning the globe. Disposal proceeds in 1996 totalled 720 million stg, including this week's sell-off of Tilcon in the U.S. to Ireland's CRH Plc for $329 million.
